verses.text: The LORD said to Moses,
"Set apart for me every firstborn male. The first male born to every mother among the people of Israel belongs to me, whether it is a person or an animal."
Then Moses said to the people, "Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, where you were slaves. The LORD brought you out of there with his mighty hand. Do not eat anything made with yeast.
Today, in the month of Abib, you are leaving.

The LORD promised your ancestors that he would give you the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey. When he brings you there, you must keep this ceremony in this month.
For seven days eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day hold a feast to honour the LORD.
Eat bread made without yeast for those seven days. Nothing with yeast in it is to be seen among you. No yeast is to be seen anywhere in your land.
On that day tell your son, 'I do this because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.'
This ceremony will be like a sign on your hand and a reminder on your forehead, so that the law of the LORD will always be on your lips. For the LORD brought you out of Egypt with his mighty hand.
So you must keep this law at the right time every year.
The LORD will bring you into the land of the Canaanites and give it to you, as he promised you and your ancestors.
Then you must give to the LORD the first male born to every mother. Every firstborn male of your animals belongs to the LORD.
You may buy back every firstborn donkey by giving a lamb in its place. If you do not buy it back, you must break its neck. And you must buy back every firstborn son among your children.
In the days to come, when your son asks you, 'What does this mean?' tell him, 'With his mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, where we were slaves.

When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, the LORD killed every firstborn in Egypt, both people and animals. That is why I sacrifice to the LORD every firstborn male animal, but I buy back each of my firstborn sons.'
It will be like a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead, because the LORD brought us out of Egypt with his mighty hand."

When Pharaoh let the people go, God did not lead them along the road through the land of the Philistines, even though it was shorter. God said, "If they face war, they might change their minds and go back to Egypt."
So God led the people the long way round, through the desert towards the Red Sea. The people of Israel left Egypt ready for battle.

Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, because Joseph had made the people of Israel promise him. He had said, "God will surely come to help you. When he does, you must carry my bones up from this place with you."
They left Succoth and camped at Etham, at the edge of the desert.
During the day the LORD went ahead of them in a pillar of cloud to show them the way. At night he went ahead of them in a pillar of fire to give them light. So they could travel by day or by night.
The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night never left its place in front of the people.
